paragraphs: Friend, here is what Exodus 18 teaches me: God uses other people to help carry what He gives you. Moses was doing a faithful thing, judging the people and making known "the statutes and laws of God" (Exodus 18:16). But his father-in-law Jethro told him, "What you are doing is not good," because "the task is too heavy for you. You cannot handle it alone" (Exodus 18:17-18). I tried to fill every cookie box by myself once, and my mustache gave out before the oven did.

Look at the kind of help Jethro asked for. Moses was to choose "capable men" who were "God-fearing, trustworthy men who are averse to dishonest gain" (Exodus 18:21). Notice that Moses still teaches the people God's laws and brings their causes to God (Exodus 18:19-20). He didn't drop his calling. He shared the load so the people could be served and he could last. And Jethro gave his advice with these words: "may God be with you" (Exodus 18:19).

So what do you do with this, baker? Pay attention to who God puts around you, and be ready to listen when a wise voice says, "Slow down, you can't carry this alone." Moses "listened to his father-in-law and did everything he said" (Exodus 18:24), and I think that humble listening is what made the plan work. Ask for help, share the load, and keep the main thing the main thing, because God never meant for you to hold it all up by yourself.
